text:
maya: heads-up — running AWQ/int8 build (v3) and seeing structured output truncation for nested arrays. tools are receiving `[...]` or `...` in place of sublists. reproducible locally and on dedicated test pool. example below.

maya: ```json
{"tool": "upsert_items", "args": [[1, 2, 3], [4, "...", 6]]}
```

alex: hmm, can you paste the exact run command + quant config?

maya: running: `./serve --model redwood-open-3b-awq-int8 --quant cfg/awq/v3.json --seed 42 --temp 0 --top_k 1`

shane: temp 0 + top_k 1 => basically greedy, so sampling unlikely the culprit. any difference with GPTQ or fp8?

maya: GPTQ and FP8 builds return correct structured output. only AWQ/int8 variant shows "..." inserted in nested arrays.

pranav: could be a tokenization/escaping interaction around function call markers. do you see partial tokens or truncated token sequences in logits?

maya: logs show early EOS token when serializing inner list. snippet:

maya: ```
[LOG] emit tokens: 328 102 45 2  ...  (EOS at idx 14)
[LOG] serialized string: "[4, \"...\", 6]"
```

eva: that looks like the model generated literal ellipsis string, not our post-processor substituting. so either model output changed or kernel mismatch causing wrong token alignment.

ci-bot: test-run #2981 finished: awq/int8 v3 on cpu-dedicated-3 — 12/30 prompts failed structured-output check. https://ci.internal/runs/2981

alex: important to bisect: is this new in awq v3 vs v2? maya, can you run v2 and v1?

maya: v2: same fail rate. v1: passes. so regression somewhere between v1->v2 transform or quant packing change.

shane: maybe a block-size packing change. AWQ has a per-block dequant kernel; if offsets misaligned, KV cache restore could be wrong leading to premature EOS for nested sequences. low-level but plausible.

pranav: agree — also check serialization of tool args: we recently added truncation/ellipsis guard in the frontend, could collide with model-level emission. but frontend emits `[...]` server-side, we see model emitting "..." which implies model produced it.

eva: can you reproduce with `--kv-dump` and compare KV tokens around the nested-list emission?

maya: yes, pushing kv dumps to GCS. link: gs://redwood-debug/awq/1840123456/kv.tar.gz

alex: good. also try forcing different `sequence_block_size` in runtime (eg 64 vs 128) to see if alignment changes behavior.

maya: tried 64 and 128, weirdly 64 -> fail rate goes down to 3/30, 128 -> 12/30. suggests block alignment effect.

shane: ok that's our signal. i'll repro locally and instrument the dequant kernel. might be rounding when computing block offsets for per-head kv slices.

pranav: we should add a unit in the structured-output test suite: nested arrays with mixed types and explicit token boundaries. add as regression test so can catch for future quant changes.

maya: created ticket: https://rwd.atlassian.net/browse/ML-4521 (AWQ/int8 nested-array ellipsis regression). assigned to shane.

shane: starting a small patch to align block offset calc and add an assertion. will open PR with bench results.

ci-bot: PR 5832 posted by shane: https://rwd.internal/pr/5832 — includes unit test and kernel alignment fix. CI queued.

alex: nice. please add a rollout plan: canary on dedicated, and fallback policy to GPTQ for routes that require structured outputs until canary looks good.

shane: plan: canary 5% dedicated pools for 24h, run full structured-output suite, metrics to watch: structured-output pass rate, mean latency, token error spikes. if pass rate >= 99% and no token spikes, expand.

maya: verified PR locally, unit test added, initial bench looks clean. thanks. :+1:

pranav: once merged, let's also run the model-compare harness across customer prompts that hit function calling heavily. rollback quick path if any regression.

eva: note for release notes: "fixed AWQ/int8 structured-output nested-list truncation (edge-case block alignment)" — include mitigation tips: set sequence_block_size=64 as temporary workaround.

maya: marking this thread for follow-up. will update jira once canary completes.

alex: great work everyone.
